clue.text: Joke about superior one, member of religious order

indicators.note: about says the joke word goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: a jest is a joke
U stands for upper class, so superior
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about a senior figure who belongs to a holy order.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jesuit belongs to the Society of Jesus, a Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola.

clue.text: Change payment arrangement if engaging a songstress

parts.note: to edit something is to change it
HP is hire purchase, a British instalment plan for paying

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the word if wraps around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Altering how instalments are paid, provided a singer is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hire purchase is the British name for buying on instalments; 'engaging' wraps the word if around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf was the celebrated French chanteuse, a singer famed for 'Non, je ne regrette rien'.

clue.text: Labour shadow cabinet was once so downtrodden

definitions.text: Labour shadow cabinet was once so
definitions.meaning: Michael Foot led the Labour Party in opposition (1980-83), so his shadow cabinet sat beneath him

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Labour's opposition team was once crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot was leader of the British Labour Party in opposition from 1980 to 1983, so his team was literally under Foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trampled lies beneath people's feet, an idiom for being oppressed or trodden on.

clue.text: Terrible con endlessly pinching silver

indicators.note: pinching means nipping hold of, so the shortened con word grips the metal
endlessly says the last letter of the word for con is dropped

parts.note: a con is a trick
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A dreadful swindle that never ends, involving stolen silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events are dreadful and calamitous, so the two adjectives share the sense of disastrous.

clue.text: Rotter longing to be helping on golf course

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a dishonourable man
dying for something means longing for it

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who is desperate to be useful out on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs, so working as one is assisting a player round the course.

clue.text: Naughty corporal's doings in US city

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters misbehave into a new order

parts.note: the letters of corporal's, keeping the s
taken as written

explanation.surface: A misbehaving NCO's activities in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of corporal's is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a large city in the American state of Colorado, home to the Air Force Academy.

clue.text: Some French couple coming to Paris finally loses hope

parts.note: des is French for some
a couple is a pair

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word Paris

explanation.surface: A French pair arriving in Paris at last gives up all hope.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to abandon hope, so the verb phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fifty trapped in a river rising somewhere in the Crimea

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top
trapped in says the numeral is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people caught in a swelling river somewhere on the Crimean peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' puts L inside A TAY to give ATLAY, which 'rising' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a resort town on the Crimean coast, famous for the 1945 conference of Allied leaders.

clue.text: A slogan — it could conjure up a feeling for days gone by

definitions.text: a feeling for days gone by

indicators.note: conjuring up is producing by magic, so these letters are magicked into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A catchphrase might summon up wistful memories of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past, a wistful emotion about earlier times.

clue.text: Such may offer various bread bits left to be eaten

definitions.text: Such may offer various bread bits left to be eaten

indicators.note: various suggests assorted, so the letters come in an assorted order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garden feeders may hold assorted crumbs put out for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird tables are raised garden platforms where scraps such as crusts are left out for wild birds.

clue.text: Continue running after the others have stopped?

definitions.meaning: to endure or carry on, as in 'the rain will not hold up'

definitions.text: running after the others have stopped?
definitions.meaning: the final runner, coming in behind everyone else

explanation.surface: Keep going, still running when everyone else has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb meaning endure; the other is the adjective for the one coming in final, behind the rest.

clue.text: More troublesome row interrupted by warning instrument

indicators.note: interrupted by says the instrument breaks into the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
a horn is sounded as a warning

explanation.surface: A noisier argument broken up by someone sounding an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a prickly, difficult one, so the comparative means harder to handle.

clue.text: Bible given to a sailor brings divine manifestation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Scripture handed to a seaman reveals a god in visible form.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief an avatar is a deity's descent to earth in bodily form, an incarnation.

clue.text: 'Go away!' Oxford said?

indicators.note: said signals the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe

explanation.surface: Someone from the university town tells an intruder to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city or university; here it is a kind of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is used to drive off animals or unwanted people, a shout of be off.

clue.text: Computer component that gives motorist a difficult experience?

definitions.meaning: the storage disk unit inside a computer

definitions.text: that gives motorist a difficult experience?
definitions.meaning: a tough journey at the wheel

explanation.surface: A piece of computer kit that makes a car trip tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer stores data on its main disk unit; read as two words, it is a tough journey behind the wheel.

clue.text: Bad girls and lovable ones

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone wrong and are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Naughty girls who are nonetheless endearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlings are dearly loved people, so endearing ones in the plural.

clue.text: International property without a particular sort of legal document

definitions.text: without a particular sort of legal document

parts.note: an estate is landed property

explanation.surface: Global real estate held without the right kind of paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Dying intestate means dying without having made a will, the legal document that disposes of property.

clue.text: Reprimanded Conservative made safe

parts.note: ensured can mean secured or made safe

explanation.surface: A Tory was told off after securing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be censured is to be formally rebuked or criticised, so both are past-tense verbs of scolding.

clue.text: Relations creating troubles — there's little right in such

indicators.note: in says the short letter goes inside the word for troubles

parts.note: to trouble someone is to bother them
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: Family members causing grief, with little justice among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothers are male siblings, so kin or family relations.

clue.text: Small mammal not initially seen? Exactly!

indicators.note: not initially seen says the opening letter of the mammal is out of sight

parts.note: a stoat is a small weasel-like mammal

explanation.surface: A little creature that went unnoticed at first, quite right!
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly or precisely, as a suit fits someone just right.

clue.text: Roadside cafe maybe found heading north or south

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up or down the grid, so it works in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A transport cafe beside a road, travelling north or south.
explanation.walkthrough: In British use a pull-up is a stopping place for drivers, such as a lorry drivers' cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport cafe is a place where drivers stop, so an example of a stopping place by the road.

clue.text: A daughter taking a long time to offer wise sayings

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: A girl who takes forever to come out with pearls of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are proverbs, traditional sayings that express a general truth.

clue.text: Servant tiring of errands to some extent?

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dogsbody somewhat weary of running little jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer is a dogsbody who runs errands for others, so a lowly helper.

clue.text: Famous Frenchman rues a sou going astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noted Frenchman regrets losing a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century philosopher of The Social Contract, a celebrated thinker.

clue.text: Warning providing by dealer trading

indicators.note: providing means supplying, so the two words supply the letters from within themselves

explanation.surface: A caution offered by a trader in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal of danger, a noun meaning a caution.

clue.text: See 2
Additional words about bad angel becoming chief troublemaker

indicators.note: about says the rider word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document

indicators.note: bad suggests corrupted, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Extra text concerning a fallen angel who turns into the main agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Additional words' is a rider, a clause tacked onto a document; 'about' wraps it round the shuffled angel, signalled by 'bad'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader heads a group of wrongdoers, the instigator of trouble.

clue.text: The fellow travels on horseback around British islands

parts.note: he is the fellow
rides means travels on horseback

explanation.surface: A man riding a horse around isles off Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the archipelagos off western Scotland, a group of islands.

clue.text: Rather attractive

explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means fairly or quite; as an adjective it means good-looking.
